name: xp_const
diagnosis: The agent commits to its first edit too early. Over 13 unedited runs (2210 episodes, 342 solved = 15.5%), within-task odds of solving by number of calls before the first edit: 0-2 calls (27% of episodes) OR 0.76; 3-4 calls (34%) OR 1.42; 5-7 calls (22%) OR 1.72; 8+ calls (17%) OR 0.12. 35.1% of edit_file calls fail, and an episode with any failed edit solves less often (OR 0.42). Earlier always-on pushes along the same direction at 0.125 gap per layer solved 28, 33, 31, 30 of 170 (pooled 17.9% vs 15.5%), but later batches showed about zero gain, and a 1.0 gap dose solved 18.
mechanism: One quiet MLP neuron in each of layers 18, 20, 22 is rewritten into an always-on unit (ridge readout q with q.x = 1.00, held-out sd 0.011-0.018; gate = 4q, up = q). Its output column writes the negative of the class-mean difference 'this call makes the first edit' minus 'this call explores' (held-out AUC 0.77-0.83), sized so the residual shifts 0.125 class gaps per layer after the MLP output normalisation. Verified from the stored bf16 tensors: shift -0.11 to -0.14 gaps at every position type, residual change 1.2-2.9% of norm, no other neuron changed.
predicted_behaviour: Mean calls before the first edit rises from about 4.8 to about 5.2 (5.0-5.6); share of episodes that edit within 2 calls falls from 27% to about 23%; edit_file failure rate falls from 35% to about 32%.

name: xp_pre
diagnosis: Same early-commit diagnosis as xp_const (0-2 calls before first edit OR 0.76, 5-7 calls OR 1.72). The always-on push also acts after the first edit, where it has no purpose: at larger always-on doses the edit failure rate fell (35% -> 31% at 0.25, 27% at 0.5) but the 8+ call bucket (OR 0.12) grew from 17% to 42% at 0.5 and 36 of 1700 episodes never edited, so the solve rate stayed near 17%.
mechanism: Same write direction and layers, but the neuron is gated: a ridge readout separates positions before the first edit from generated positions after it (held-out AUC 0.993-0.996; fires above 1 on 86-88% of before positions and 1.1-1.4% of after positions). Dose 0.25 gaps per layer while it is on. Verified: shift -0.22 to -0.31 gaps before the first edit, 0.000 at post-edit decision positions (-0.19 to -0.21 at post-edit prompt positions, which the gate was not fitted on).
predicted_behaviour: Mean calls before the first edit rises from about 4.8 to about 6.0 (5.5-6.8); the 8+ call share rises from 17% to about 23%; calls after the first edit per episode stay within 10% of base.

name: xp_think
diagnosis: Same early-commit diagnosis. The always-on push changes the residual at every prompt token (tool output, file content: 1.4-2.4% of norm at 0.125), where no decision is made; that may be a pure cost. The decision is taken at generated positions (direction AUC 0.77-0.83 at the first generated token, 0.99 at the token before the tool call).
mechanism: Same write direction and layers, gated to generated positions (thinking and tool-call tokens, before and after the first edit) versus prompt positions (held-out AUC 0.961-0.966; fires above 1 on about 82% of generated and 5-7% of prompt positions). Dose 0.25 gaps per layer while on. Verified: shift -0.29 to -0.35 gaps at decision positions, -0.11 to -0.21 at mid-thinking positions, -0.002 to -0.006 at prompt positions (residual change 0.1-0.2% there).
predicted_behaviour: Mean calls before the first edit rises from about 4.8 to about 5.6 (5.1-6.5); edit_file failure rate falls from 35% to about 31%.

name: xp_early
diagnosis: The relation between exploration and solving is an inverted U: 0-2 calls before the first edit OR 0.76, 3-4 calls OR 1.42, 5-7 calls OR 1.72, 8+ calls OR 0.12 (2.7% solved). A uniform push moves every episode right, including those already past the peak. This is correlational evidence only; it is the least tested idea here.
mechanism: Same write direction and layers, gated on how far the episode has gone: on at decision positions with agent-call index <= 4, off at index >= 8 and after the first edit (held-out AUC 0.95-0.97). Verified shift: -0.43 to -0.54 gaps at first-token positions of calls <= 4, -0.02 to -0.04 at calls 5-7, 0.000 at calls >= 8 and after the first edit; about -0.10 at prompt positions. Residual change at early calls is 4-14% of norm, the largest of the five.
predicted_behaviour: Share of episodes that edit within 2 calls falls from 27% to about 15% (10-22%); the 8+ call share stays below 22% (base 17%).

name: xp_const_ctrl
diagnosis: Control for xp_const: tests whether a gain comes from the direction or from adding any always-on neuron of this size. An earlier matched control solved 14.7% (base 15.5%) and still raised calls before the first edit to 5.1.
mechanism: Identical neurons, gate and up rows as xp_const; the output column is a random direction (seed 7), sized so the mean residual change equals that of xp_const (measured 1.1-1.7% vs 1.2-2.9% of norm at the decision position). Verified shift along the explore direction: within 0.006 gaps of zero.
predicted_behaviour: Mean calls before the first edit within 0.4 of base (about 4.8); edit_file failure rate within 2 points of 35%.
build_command: CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES= OMP_NUM_THREADS=8 /path/to/gemma-v2/tii-venv/bin/python code/build.py --edit xp_const_ctrl   (run after xp_const: it reads edits/xp_const/report.json)
